## What's changed

- Preserves HDR automatically as 10-bit video with the source color signaling during library optimization.
- Keeps Dolby Vision protected and untouched by default.
- When Dolby Vision protection is disabled, preserves already-efficient Dolby Vision video instead of converting it unnecessarily, including track-cleanup-only jobs.
- Converts Dolby Vision to validated 10-bit BT.2020/PQ HDR10 only when the selected codec policy already requires a full video transcode.
- Adds an exact FFmpeg libplacebo, Vulkan, and target-encoder capability check for the Dolby Vision-to-HDR10 pipeline.
- Validates that converted output is 10-bit HDR10 and no longer contains Dolby Vision metadata before replacing the source.
- Updates the optimizer interface and analysis summary to distinguish preserved Dolby Vision media from files that require HDR10 conversion.
- Verifies that Docker and macOS release FFmpeg bundles include the required Dolby Vision rendering support.

Library Optimization remains optional and server-managed; existing players do not require an update.
